name: oversight
description: Strength of actual oversight of the application owner (index; 0 = none, 1 = full)
source: No documentary value; range chosen to span absent to moderate oversight. Weak oversight under current practice is described by SFMTA staff (SFMTA staff, personal communication, 2026).
notes: Enters the start log-odds as b_ov x oversight (code/model.py, Sim.p_start). PW3 adds 0.3 at the start, capped at 1 (Sim._accountability_on).

name: b0
description: Intercept of the monthly start probability: baseline log-odds that the owner starts preparing an application in an open window
source: No documentary value; range chosen so that the baseline monthly start probability spans about 0.1% to 5.2% (logit -6.9 to -2.9).
notes: Sim.p_start. A start is possible only in an open window (local: January-June; HSIP: July-October of a cycle year), when the task is idle and not blocked by deflection (Sim._task_step). Tasks committed by a pathway to an HSIP cycle start without this draw, and may start before July (see d_split).

name: b_own
description: Change in start log-odds when a named owner is in post
source: No documentary value; range includes 0 so that a null effect is admissible.
notes: Owner indicator (Sim.owner): historical segment 1 until the dedicated SG105 funds end (2024-06, fixed in code), then 0 under M-A and M-D and 1 otherwise; projection 0 under M-A and M-D and 1 otherwise; forced to 1 under PW3; 0 while the post is vacant (lam_quit, t_vac).

name: b_spec
description: Change in start log-odds when a written deadline with consequences applies to applying for funds
source: No documentary value; range includes 0. The APS policy sets installation deadlines only after funding is secured and sets none for applying (SFMTA, 2022a, p. 2).
notes: Deadline indicator is 0 under current practice and 1 under PW3 (Sim._accountability_on).

name: b_ov
description: Change in start log-odds per unit of oversight
source: No documentary value; range includes 0.
notes: Sim.p_start.

name: b_pr
description: Change in start log-odds per unit of accumulated advocacy pressure
source: No documentary value; range includes 0.
notes: Pressure = sum over retained pressure events of exp(-(t - t_i)/k_decay) (Sim.pressure).

name: b_enf
description: Change in start log-odds per external-enforcement level above level 1
source: No documentary value; range includes 0.
notes: Enforcement levels: 0 none, 1 latent (initial), 2 structured negotiation, 3 lawsuit, 4 court order; the term is b_enf x max(0, level - 1) (Sim.p_start). Levels rise by eps_enf events and, under PW3, by the th_idle signposts.

name: lam_press
description: Rate of advocacy pressure events directed at the agency
source: No documentary value; range 0-0.5 events per year. In the public records searched, no 2026 public comment to the SFMTA Board and no speaker at the July 2026 Mayor's Disability Council meeting addressed APS (Mayor's Disability Council, 2026); meetings outside the public record are unobserved.
notes: Converted to a monthly probability 1 - exp(-lam/12). PW3 doubles the rate at the start. No events occur during quiet spells (lam_quiet, t_quiet). Under M-A and M-D an event is deflected with probability p_deflect instead of adding pressure.

name: k_decay
description: Decay time constant of advocacy pressure
source: No documentary value.
notes: Each retained event contributes exp(-(t - t_i)/k_decay) (Sim.pressure).

name: p_deflect
description: Probability that a pressure event is answered by pointing to cost or another funder (buck-passing) instead of adding pressure
source: No documentary value; range set high (0.5-0.95) because SFMTA's 2026 presentation to the Mayor's Disability Council answers APS questions with cost (three pages on technical challenges and cost) and states that remaining requests are "selected based on funding" (SFMTA, 2026a, pp. 4-6, 8), and SFMTA staff describe responsibility being passed between agencies (SFMTA staff, personal communication, 2026). The rule form follows buck-passing in the garbage-can model (Fioretti & Lomi, 2010).
notes: Active only in M-A and M-D (code/model.py, switches); sampled but without effect in other settings. A deflection blocks idle tasks for r_back months; the named target (SFCTA, General Fund, Caltrans) is drawn uniformly and appears only in the event log.

name: r_back
description: Months before a deflected idle task can start again
source: No documentary value.
notes: Active only in M-A and M-D. Truncated to whole months (int).

name: d_prep
description: Months needed to prepare an application
source: No documentary value.
notes: Rounded to whole months. Preparation not finished by the window deadline (local: June; HSIP: November of the cycle year) is recorded as missed and not carried over (Sim._task_step). Also sets when the first HSIP application instance is ready and, with d_split, how early a committed HSIP task starts.

name: m_b
description: Reduction in start log-odds per unit of staffing strain
source: No documentary value. The constraint itself is documented: Signal Shop staffing is "often the limiting factor" in delivery (SFCTA, 2023b, p. 9), and SFMTA slowed hiring from July 2024 and froze non-essential hiring from October 2024 (SFMTA, 2025).
notes: Active only in M-B1, M-B2 and M-D. Strain starts at a month fixed by setting (2024-07 for M-B1 and M-D; 2023-01 for M-B2; not sampled) and rises linearly to 1 over strain_ramp months (Sim.strain).

name: strain_ramp
description: Months for staffing strain to rise from 0 to 1
source: No documentary value.
notes: Active only in M-B1, M-B2 and M-D.

name: strain_end
description: Months after December 2026 at which staffing strain ends
source: No documentary value; no document states when the hiring restrictions end. The restrictions themselves are documented (SFMTA, 2025).
notes: Active only in M-B1, M-B2 and M-D. Truncated to whole months; strain is 0 from 2026-12 + strain_end onward (Sim.strain).

name: phi
description: Fraction by which full staffing strain reduces in-house crew capacity
source: No documentary value.
notes: Active only in M-B1, M-B2 and M-D. Capacity = k0 x (1 - phi x strain) (Sim._deliver).

name: k0
description: In-house crew capacity for request-channel installations
source: No documentary value; range 0.5-3.0 sites per month. While dedicated funds were available the request lists record 23 in-house installations between January 2023 and August 2024 (about 14 per year, 1.2 per month) (SFMTA, 2020–2026); this is treated as observed throughput, not a capacity bound.
notes: Capacity accrues monthly into a bank capped at max(3 x capacity, 1) sites; each installation uses one unit (Sim._deliver).

name: h_in
description: Rate at which a funded in-house site (Fi) is installed, given crew capacity
source: SFMTA request status lists (SFMTA, 2020–2026), training period July 2022 to February 2025: 23 Fi-to-installed transitions before the August 2024 breakpoint, about 0.96 per year; the range approximates the central 95% interval of that estimate.
notes: Design documentation differed: it specified sampling from a Gamma(23.5, 294.7 site-months) estimate (95% interval about 0.61-1.38 per year); the code samples uniformly on 0.59-1.41. The same transitions inform the screening targets, so screening is not independent of this range; a separate screening run used U(0.3, 2.0). Monthly probability 1 - exp(-h_in/12); only sites past their design-complete month are eligible.

name: h_fs
description: Rate at which a site funded through a signal project (Fs) is installed with that project
source: SFMTA request status lists (SFMTA, 2020–2026), training period July 2022 to February 2025: 9 Fs-to-installed transitions; the range approximates the central 95% interval of the estimated rate (about 0.08-0.30 per year).
notes: Design documentation differed: it specified sampling from a Gamma(9.5, 657.7 site-months) estimate (mean about 0.17 per year); the code samples uniformly on 0.08-0.31 with default 0.16. A separate screening run used U(0.03, 0.5). Sites whose parent project is unfunded, or (fs5_parent = 0) unidentified, never install by this route.

name: m_c
description: Reduction in start log-odds per unit of cost pressure
source: No documentary value. SFMTA states that the easier intersections have been completed and the remaining ones are harder and more expensive (SFMTA, 2024a).
notes: Active only in M-C1 and M-D. Cost pressure = (unit cost - $20,000) / $20,000 (Sim.costpress).

name: g_cost
description: Annual growth rate of the base APS unit cost
source: Range 0-0.15 per year brackets the growth implied by SFMTA's reported minimum per-site cost: $20,000 in 2018 (SFMTA, 2018a, slide 6), $30,000 in 2023 (SFMTA, 2023, pp. 4-5) and $40,000 in 2026 (SFMTA, 2026a, pp. 4-5), about 9% per year; the lower end admits no growth.
notes: Active only in M-C1 and M-D; growth compounds from July 2022 (Sim.unit_cost). In other settings the unit cost stays at u0.

name: tau
description: Share of candidate (C) sites that are technically blocked from installation
source: No documentary value. Qualitative basis: SFMTA, 2024a (remaining intersections are harder).
notes: Active only in M-C2 and M-D; drawn once per C site when it is created. Blocked sites are excluded from every route: local batches, HSIP bundles, set-aside applications, the PW5 design rule and in-house installation (Sim._local_decision, Sim._build_app, Sim._setaside, Sim._design_rule, Sim._deliver).

name: u0
description: Base APS cost per site where poles and conduit are adequate (July 2022 dollars)
source: Range spans two documented values that conflict: the FY2027-2031 capital programme line SG142 ($488,144 for 22 sites, about $22,000 per site; SFMTA, 2026c) and the $40,000 minimum per site reported to the Mayor's Disability Council (SFMTA, 2026a, pp. 4-5). The upper end ($50,000) is an assumption.
notes: Used for local batches, HSIP bundles (APS component), set-aside applications and the PW5 design rule (Sim.unit_cost).

name: q_pipe
description: Probability that a site needs conduit work (adds $200,000)
source: Amount documented: about $200,000 when conduit is damaged (SFMTA, 2026a, pp. 4-5). No documentary value for the probability; range 0-1.
notes: Drawn once when a site is created and counted once in planned cost (Sim._site).

name: q_ramp
description: Probability that a site needs new curb ramps (adds $200,000)
source: Amount documented: about $200,000 when excavation triggers new curb ramps (SFMTA, 2026a, pp. 4-5). No documentary value for the probability; range 0-1.
notes: Drawn once when a site is created and counted once in planned cost (Sim._site). Curb ramps within a bundled HSIP project are eligible costs (Caltrans, 2026d, Q4).

name: a_local
description: Local funds available for APS per year under current practice (no standing line)
source: Range from 0 to the largest General Fund APS line in SFMTA capital plans: $570,000 (SG143, FY2031 estimate; SFMTA, 2026c); the FY2025-2029 plan shows $292,817 for FY2028 (SFMTA, 2024b).
notes: Allocated at the July decision only if staff submitted a local application on time and no standing line is on (Sim._local_decision). One-time amounts (q_dir, a_sg017) are allocated on their own and do not release a_local. Sites are funded in priority order while cumulative cost x (1 + k_cont) fits the amount.

name: a_line
description: Annual size of a standing local line when it is on
source: No documentary value; range $0.5M-$2.0M per year. For scale, the 2023 Prop L programme for signs and signals commits about $2.8M per year in FY2026-2028 across all signal items (SFCTA, 2023b, p. 14).
notes: APS receives a_line x aps_share per year while the line is on. The line is on from the start if sw_line = 1; PW4 turns it on at the start; PW5 turns it on at month 24 if design-rule installations are below th_rule; PW1 turns it on after an approved Prop L amendment; PW2 and PW6 after an approved Prop L amendment or General Fund request. In the approval variant PW4 and PW5 request the line through the same approval chain instead. Under PW1 a Director reallocation (q_dir) provides a one-time amount equal to a_line.

name: aps_share
description: Share of a standing local line allocated to APS
source: No documentary value; range 0-0.5.
notes: Projection only; see a_line.

name: y_win
description: Crash-history window used in the HSIP benefit calculation
source: Analytical choice: 3-year (2023-2025) or 5-year (2021-2025) window ending before the Cycle 13 decision; both are sampled with equal probability. Crash counts are from DataSF injury crash records (CCSF, n.d.).
notes: Cycle 13 uses observed counts in the window; later cycles draw Poisson counts from each site's 2021-2025 annual rate (Sim._site_bcr_parts).

name: l_rule
description: Rule for the service life of a multi-countermeasure site (0 = shortest life, 1 = equal-weight mean)
source: Analytical choice approximating the HSIP Analyzer, whose treatment of mixed service lives was not verified; both rules are sampled. Service lives per countermeasure follow the Local Roadway Safety Manual (Caltrans, 2026g) (SI02 10 years, SI07 20, SI18PB 20, SI22PB 10).
notes: Sim._site_bcr_parts.

name: c_final
description: Final HSIP funding cutoff (benefit-cost ratio) in a cycle
source: Historical final cutoffs ranged from 3.5 to 18.0 in Cycles 8-12 (Caltrans, 2026d, Q69; Caltrans, 2026f, slide 22). The default (8.0) is an assumption.
notes: Approval requires BCR >= max(5.0, c_final); 5.0 is the Cycle 13 submission minimum (Caltrans, 2026c, p. 4; Caltrans, 2026d, Q65). Set-aside applications are not subject to it.

name: r_other
description: Other San Francisco HSIP requests that use part of the $10M per-agency cap
source: No documentary value; range $0-$10M. For scale, San Francisco submitted one application of $3.97M in Cycle 12 (Caltrans, 2024a). Per-agency cap: Caltrans, 2026c, p. 4; Caltrans, 2026d, Q60-61.
notes: The cap available to APS bundles is max(0, $10M - r_other), shared across the bundles of one submission (Sim._submit_hsip).

name: rho_flag
description: Probability that another San Francisco HSIP project carries a red flag at an eligibility review
source: No documentary value. The rule that delayed projects make an agency ineligible is documented (Caltrans, 2026c, p. 1; Caltrans, 2026d, Q45-54).
notes: Drawn once per review month and shared by all applications reviewed that month (Sim._agency_flagged). The agency is also flagged when its road safety plan is not valid (lrsp_until) or a modelled project has missed a milestone.

name: q_fail
description: Probability of residual random failure after an application passes the cutoff
source: No documentary value; default 0 is the no-additional-attrition control. The historical overall selection rate (62-87% in Cycles 9-12; Caltrans, 2026f, slide 22) already includes competitive attrition and is not used as a multiplier.
notes: Design documentation differed: it specified 0 for the control and U(0, 0.2) otherwise; the code samples U(0, 0.2) with default 0.

name: p_sa
description: Probability that San Francisco's pedestrian-crossing set-aside application is funded
source: No documentary value; not calibrated. Set-aside priority goes first to agencies without awards in Cycles 11-12; San Francisco holds earlier BCR awards and is placed in the second tier (Caltrans, 2026c, p. 5; Caltrans, 2026a). Per-agency limit $360,000 (Caltrans, 2026c, pp. 4-6).
notes: A set-aside instance is formed only in repack mode when preparation time allows an extra instance; total <= $400,000 and APS <= 20% of total (Sim._setaside).

name: s_12in_C
description: Share of candidate (C) sites that still have 8-inch signal heads, so a 12-inch upgrade (SI02) can carry APS
source: Signal intersection diagrams for sampled pending sites (SFMTA, n.d.-c): 7 of 15 candidate sites have 8-inch heads (0.47); the range 0.25-0.70 reflects the small sample.
notes: Drawn once per site (Sim._draw_carriers).

name: s_bp
description: Share of sites that can take backplates (backplate-only SI02)
source: No documentary value; backplates are assumed feasible almost everywhere.
notes: Backplate-only SI02 is used only in repack mode (Sim._site_bcr_parts).

name: s_mast
description: Share of full-upgrade (N) sites now pedestal-mounted, so mast-arm conversion (SI07) applies
source: No documentary value; range 0-1. Projects that add mast arms must claim SI07, not SI02 (Caltrans, 2026g).
notes: Drawn once per site; used for N sites in repack mode.

name: s_lpi
description: Share of sites where a new leading pedestrian interval (SI22PB) is possible
source: No documentary value; leading-interval status is not public for any pending site (timing cards are available only through a public-records request; SFMTA, n.d.-c).
notes: Drawn once per site.

name: c_12in
description: Cost of a 12-inch signal head upgrade per site
source: No documentary value for a 12-inch upgrade alone. Anchor: the FY2024 SG015 visibility-upgrade scope covers 8 intersections with 12-inch heads and 20 with backplates for $400,000, about $14,000 per site on average across both treatments (SFCTA, 2023b, pp. 86-92); the range is centred near this mixed-project average.
notes: Carrier cost in C-site bundles (Sim._site_bcr_parts).

name: c_bp
description: Cost of signal backplates per site
source: No documentary value.
notes: Carrier cost for backplate-only SI02 (repack mode).

name: c_lpi
description: Cost of a new leading pedestrian interval per site (signal retiming)
source: No documentary value.
notes: Also an eligible item in the set-aside total.

name: c_full
description: Total cost of a full signal upgrade per site, including poles, conduit, ramps and APS hardware
source: No documentary value for a typical site. For scale, Traffic Signals Contract 35 implies about $314,000 per site in Prop L funds and about $1.07M per site across all phases (17 sites; SFCTA, 2025b, pp. 3, 26-27).
notes: Design documentation cited a Contract 35 figure of about $554,000 per site as the upper anchor; that figure could not be traced to a page of a public document. APS hardware is included; no APS cost is added (Sim._site_bcr_parts).

name: sw_pe
description: Switch: HSIP funds preliminary engineering, so the PE authorization milestone applies
source: Rule documented: when HSIP funds design, PE authorization is due within 9 months of approval (Caltrans, 2021a, p. 8). Whether San Francisco would request design funds is unknown; both states are sampled.
notes: If 1, design and the public interest finding start after t_pe; a PE authorization later than 9 months raises a red flag (Sim._new_project).

name: t_pe
description: Months from project start to PE authorization (E-76) when HSIP funds design
source: No documentary value.
notes: Used only when sw_pe = 1. Project start is the January after approval.

name: t_pif
description: Months to obtain a public interest finding for in-house (force-account) construction
source: Requirement documented (Caltrans, 2026e, pp. 7-8); No documentary value for the duration.
notes: Runs alongside design; construction authorization waits for it (Sim._new_project).

name: q_pif_deny
description: Probability that the public interest finding is denied, so construction is contracted out
source: No documentary value.
notes: Denial does not delay construction authorization; it adds t_contract months and a cost gap of (k_contract - 1) x project cost to be funded by top-up (Sim._project_step).

name: sw_consult
description: Switch: consultant design, which extends the construction-authorization limit from 36 to 42 months
source: Rule documented (Caltrans, 2021a, p. 8; Caltrans, 2026f, slide 23); which design route San Francisco would use is unknown; both states are sampled.
notes: A construction authorization later than the limit raises a red flag (Sim._new_project).

name: t_con_med
description: Median months from project start to construction authorization (E-76)
source: San Francisco HSIP projects took 15-28 months from award to construction authorization (Cycles 6, 10 and 11; Caltrans, 2026a); subtracting the 8-10 months between award and the model's project start gives 8-16 months.
notes: Drawn per project as t_con_med x exp(0.40 Z), Z standard normal (log-normal; sigma 0.40 fixed in code, right tail not truncated), and never earlier than design completion or the public interest finding (Sim._new_project). Project start is the January after approval.

name: d_split
description: Extra preparation months for each additional application instance
source: No documentary value.
notes: Instance i is ready at start + d_prep + i x d_split; bundles not ready by the deadline are dropped, and a set-aside is added only if an extra instance is ready (Sim._submit_hsip). A task committed to an HSIP cycle may start from ceil(d_prep + (m - 1) x d_split) months before the November deadline (m = 1 for an SG015 bundle, 3 for a repack), and otherwise from the July window (Sim._task_step).

name: t_des
description: Months from a local award to design completion, when cost overruns are found
source: No documentary value.
notes: Rounded to whole months; also the earliest installation month for locally funded sites (Sim._local_decision).

name: t_dsg
description: Months from HSIP design start (PE authorization or project start) to design completion
source: No documentary value.
notes: Overruns on HSIP projects are drawn at design completion (Sim._project_step).

name: t_pause
description: Months a project pauses when a contracting cost gap is not funded
source: No documentary value.
notes: After the pause one more top-up request is made; if refused, the project terminates (Sim._project_step).

name: k_cont
description: Contingency budgeted as a share of planned cost
source: No documentary value.
notes: Local batches are sized on cost x (1 + k_cont); HSIP application cost includes contingency; overruns are first absorbed by contingency (Sim._local_decision, Sim._build_app, Sim._overruns).

name: crash_impute
description: Treatment of crashes at sites without a crash match (0 exclude from HSIP, 1 median, 2 90th percentile of matched sites)
source: Analytical choice; all three treatments are sampled. One of the 76 pending sites has no crash match in the injury crash records (CCSF, n.d.).
notes: Applies to that site and to new requests that copy its attributes (Sim._impute).

name: lrsp_until
description: Months after July 2026 until San Francisco's local road safety plan (or equivalent) lapses for HSIP eligibility; negative = already lapsed
source: Rule documented: a plan updated or confirmed within five years is required (Caltrans, 2026c, p. 1; Caltrans, 2026d, Q45-54). San Francisco's plan date was not verified; range -6 to 54 months.
notes: When the plan lapses an update starts; it finishes after t_lrsp months and succeeds with q_lrsp, giving 60 more months; a failed update restarts (Sim._lrsp_valid). The requirement that an update finish before the review date is an assumption.

name: q_lrsp
description: Probability that a plan update succeeds
source: No documentary value.
notes: See lrsp_until.

name: t_lrsp
description: Months to complete a plan update
source: No documentary value.
notes: See lrsp_until.

name: c_xing
description: Cost per site of a signalized crossing upgrade (SI19PB) in a set-aside application
source: No documentary value.
notes: Used for a set-aside site only when neither new countdown heads nor a new leading interval applies (Sim._setaside).

name: t_ext
description: Length of the single extension allowed after five years without construction
source: Rule documented: projects without construction authorization after five years are removed and funds returned (Caltrans, 2021a, p. 8; Caltrans, 2026f, slide 23). No documentary value for the extension length.
notes: See e_ext (Sim._project_step).

name: lam_hw
description: Rate of push-button or signal-hardware change events per candidate site (PW5 design rule)
source: No documentary value.
notes: Used only in PW5; a change event at a C site funds APS if the annual add-on budget (b_hw) covers it, moving the site to the in-house queue (Fi), where installation remains subject to h_in and crew capacity (Sim._design_rule, Sim._deliver).

name: b_hw
description: Annual maintenance budget for APS add-ons under the PW5 design rule
source: No documentary value.
notes: Used only in PW5; reset each July.

name: q_sg017_block
description: Probability that an SG017 hardware-replacement allocation request excludes new APS
source: No documentary value. SG017's capital-programme scope includes new APS where poles and conduit are adequate (SFMTA, 2026c), but recorded SG017 allocations went to other hardware, most recently about 98 signal controllers in FY2025-26 (SFCTA, 2025b, p. 7).
notes: Used only in PW6; requests in July 2026 and July 2027. A first exclusion moves PW6 to a Prop L amendment (Sim._pathway_signposts).

name: a_sg017
description: SG017 funds usable for APS per year (FY2027, FY2028)
source: Range 0-$250,000 is up to half of SG017's $500,000 per year in FY2027 and FY2028 (SFMTA, 2026c); the share is an assumption.
notes: Used only in PW6; a one-time amount allocated at the next July local decision, on its own (it does not release a_local).

name: s_cd
description: Share of sites with unknown countdown status that lack countdown heads
source: No documentary value; range 0-0.2 because SFMTA reports that nearly all signalized intersections have countdown heads (SFMTA, 2024a). The 10 sites identified as missing them are set from data.
notes: Drawn once per site; sets eligibility for SI18PB (Sim._draw_carriers).

name: c_cd
description: Cost of new pedestrian countdown heads per site
source: No documentary value.
notes: Used in bundles (repack mode) and set-aside totals.

name: sigma_over
description: Log-scale of cost overruns found at design completion
source: No documentary value.
notes: Actual cost = planned x exp(sigma_over x Z). For local batches actual cost is capped at $1.5M, the documented per-site upper end (SFMTA, 2026a, pp. 4-5); for HSIP projects it is not capped (Sim._overruns, Sim._project_step).

name: lam_quiet
description: Rate at which advocacy quiet spells start
source: No documentary value.
notes: A quiet spell lasts t_quiet months (failure event F-m).

name: t_fix
description: Months to clear a red flag after a missed milestone
source: No documentary value.
notes: A late PE authorization flags the agency from month 9 after project start until PE authorization + t_fix; a late construction authorization from the 36- or 42-month limit until construction authorization + t_fix; several flags merge into one interval from the earliest start to the latest end; a flag stops counting when its project terminates. Truncated to whole months (Sim._new_project).

name: t_contract
description: Months to procure a contractor after a denied public interest finding
source: No documentary value.
notes: See q_pif_deny.

name: k_contract
description: Contractor cost as a multiple of in-house cost
source: No documentary value.
notes: The gap (k_contract - 1) x project cost must be funded by top-up.

name: q_topup
description: Probability that a funding gap (overrun beyond contingency or contracting gap) receives a top-up allocation
source: No documentary value.
notes: Without top-up a locally funded site returns to candidate status and an HSIP project terminates (Sim._overruns, Sim._project_step). Labelled stage "projection" in code/params.py, but local overruns also occur in the historical segment, where this parameter is used; in projections it is redrawn independently rather than taken from the screened combinations.

name: t_partner
description: Delay of the partner project that carries APS in an SG015 bundle
source: No documentary value.
notes: Added to construction authorization for sg015-mode projects (PW1, PW4).

name: q_partner_cancel
description: Probability that the partner project is cancelled
source: No documentary value.
notes: Cancellation occurs six months after project start and terminates the APS project (failure event F-g).

name: lam_quit
description: Rate at which the application owner leaves the post
source: No documentary value.
notes: Monthly probability 1 - exp(-lam_quit/12) (failure event F-h).

name: t_vac
description: Months the owner's post stays vacant
source: No documentary value.
notes: Rounded to whole months; the owner indicator is 0 while vacant.

name: q_drop
description: Probability that an application in preparation is dropped when the owner leaves
source: No documentary value.
notes: Applied to each task in preparation.

name: q_veto
description: Probability that the SFCTA Board rejects a Prop L amendment adding an APS line
source: No documentary value.
notes: Decided three months after the request (Sim._propl_amendment). Used in PW1, PW2 and PW6 (and PW4 and PW5 in the approval variant).

name: t_defer
description: Months a Prop L amendment is deferred before a decision
source: No documentary value. For scale, an SFCTA allocation whose scope includes APS was approved about 3.5 months after the November 2024 election that led to it (SFCTA, 2025c).
notes: Rounded to whole months; the decision falls at request + 3 + t_defer months, and a deferral longer than th_defer counts as failure.

name: q_gf
description: Probability that a General Fund request for an APS line is included in the budget
source: No documentary value.
notes: Decided in the next July after the request. Used in PW2 and PW6 (and PW4 and PW5 in the approval variant).

name: q_dir
description: Probability that a Director reallocation is used for APS
source: No documentary basis for a discretionary allocation: the 10% figure in SFMTA's capital budget resolution is the threshold above which cumulative technical or clerical corrections require Board review, not a discretionary allowance (SFMTA Board of Directors, 2026). Both the probability and the amount (a_line, once) are hypothetical.
notes: Used only at the last PW1 step, after a failed Prop L amendment; the one-time amount (a_line) is allocated at the next July local decision on its own.

name: t_quiet
description: Months an advocacy quiet spell lasts
source: No documentary value.
notes: Truncated to whole months.

name: th_defer
description: Signpost: longest acceptable Prop L deferral before switching route (months)
source: Design choice of the adaptive pathways (signposts and switching; Haasnoot et al., 2013); No documentary value; swept as a parameter.
notes: PW1, PW2, PW6 (and PW4 and PW5 in the approval variant).

name: th_idle
description: Signpost: months without a submitted application before PW3 escalates
source: Design choice (Haasnoot et al., 2013); No documentary value; swept as a parameter.
notes: Used only in PW3: first escalation to structured negotiation (enforcement level 2), then, if nothing is funded after another th_idle months, a lawsuit (level 3).

name: th_parent
description: Signpost: months of parent-project delay before PW4 moves a fold-in site to the local queue
source: Design choice (Haasnoot et al., 2013); No documentary value; swept as a parameter.
notes: Used only in PW4.

name: th_rule
description: Signpost: design-rule installations within two years below which PW5 adds a standing line
source: Design choice (Haasnoot et al., 2013); No documentary value; swept as a parameter.
notes: Used only in PW5, at month 24.

name: t_build
description: Months from construction authorization to installation for contracted-out projects
source: No documentary value; no comparable peer data.
notes: In-house HSIP projects join the crew queue at construction authorization instead (Sim._new_project).

name: e_ext
description: Probability that a one-time extension is granted at five years without construction
source: No documentary value. Rule documented (Caltrans, 2021a, p. 8).
notes: Without extension the project is removed, its sites return to their state before the award, and 10% of its cost is recorded as refunded (Sim._project_step). A project counts against agency eligibility from five years after start until construction authorization or termination (Sim._agency_flagged).

name: t_parent
description: Delay of the corridor design project that adds APS under PW4
source: No documentary value.
notes: Labelled stage "all" in code/params.py but used only at the PW4 start: corridor sites join corridor design with probability pi_scope and become installable after t_parent months (Sim._init_pathway).

name: pi_scope
description: Probability that a fold-in site of likely or unverified status is still within its parent project scope
source: No documentary value; parent-project status of each fold-in site from project pages and capital documents (see data dictionary).
notes: Sites falling out of scope become candidates (C). Under PW4 also the probability that a corridor site joins corridor design.

name: done3_real
description: Switch: the three sites whose parent signal work is complete are truly undelivered (1) rather than delivered but not yet recorded (0)
source: Parent signal work completed 2023-04-25, 2025-02-27 and 2025-05-02 while the sites remain listed as pending (SFMTA, 2020–2026); which reading is correct is unknown; both states are sampled.
notes: Design documentation listed equal probabilities; the code samples 0 and 1 with equal probability, default 1. Labelled stage "all" but used only at the projection start: 1 = in-house hand-off (Fi), 0 = installed before the start.

name: fs5_parent
description: Switch: the five signal-project (Fs) sites without an identified parent project do have one
source: SFMTA lists five sites as pending a funded signal project, but no matching project was found in public capital documents (SFMTA, 2020–2026; SFMTA, 2026c); both states are sampled.
notes: If 0, these sites never install by the signal-project route.

name: lam_arr
description: Rate of new APS requests entering the list
source: Range of first-observed requests per year in the SFMTA request status lists (SFMTA, 2020–2026): 6-17.
notes: Poisson count with monthly mean lam_arr/12. New requests take state C, Fs or N with probabilities 32/41, 6/41 and 3/41 (historical arrivals) and copy rank and crash attributes from a randomly chosen pending site (Sim._arrivals). Historical arrivals are read from data instead.

name: eps_enf
description: Rate at which external enforcement steps up one level
source: No documentary value; no local base rate. No suit or settlement against San Francisco on APS since 2010 was found in the sources searched; range 0-0.1 per year.
notes: Monthly probability eps_enf/12; maximum level 4.

name: sw_si02
description: Switch: a signal-hardware upgrade (SI02) is accepted as the carrier for APS in an HSIP application
source: Basis is an interview with SFMTA staff only (SFMTA staff, personal communication, 2026); no public Caltrans determination. APS-only projects are ineligible (Caltrans, 2026d, Q3). Default 1 is the main scenario; 0 is a robustness check.
notes: If 0, C sites cannot enter BCR bundles (Sim._site_bcr_parts).

name: sw_si07
description: Switch: mast-arm conversion (SI07) is usable as the carrier for APS at full-upgrade sites
source: SI07 is a listed countermeasure (all crashes, crash reduction factor 30%, 20-year life; Caltrans, 2026g). Default 1; 0 is a robustness check.
notes: Applies to N sites in repack mode.

name: f_aff
description: Share of crashes within 50 m that fall on the upgraded approaches (influence area of SI02/SI07)
source: No documentary value; the countermeasure applies only to upgraded approaches (Caltrans, 2026g, SI02 note), which cannot be identified crash by crash.
notes: Crashes inside the share receive all countermeasures; the rest receive only the pedestrian-crossing measures (Sim._site_bcr_parts).

name: sw_line
description: Switch: a standing local APS line is on from the projection start
source: Current practice has no standing line (SFMTA, 2026c; SFCTA, 2023b, p. 14); both states are sampled.
notes: Design documentation listed 1 as the main scenario; the code default is 0, and the main pathway comparison, a secondary analysis of the E3 runs, uses only combinations with sw_line = 0. Ignored in the historical segment.
